This page emphasizes **what I have built or implemented**, complementing the scientific questions described on the Research page. I developed an in-house flow-cell platform using a design-to-test workflow: **SolidWorks CAD → resin additive manufacturing → Nomad CNC / graphite machining → assembly → electrochemical testing** The platform supports controlled studies of suspension-electrode transport and electrochemical performance.
ADD PHOTO SET: 1. SolidWorks rendering 2. printed / machined components 3. assembled flow cell 4. operating experimental setup
**Skills demonstrated:** CAD, rapid prototyping, graphite machining, experimental design, electrochemical testing, troubleshooting. ## Taylor–Couette Electrochemical Platform Designed a customized Taylor–Couette configuration for controlled suspension-flow and transport measurements, with emphasis on separating hydrodynamic and electrochemical effects.
ADD: Taylor–Couette CAD + photograph + one representative mass-transfer result
**Skills demonstrated:** rheology, suspension mechanics, experimental hardware design, electrochemistry, transport analysis. ## Yield-Stress Rotating-Flow Modeling Developed reduced-order numerical models and finite-element simulations for rotating Newtonian, Bingham, and Herschel–Bulkley flows. Key computational elements include: - nonlinear boundary-value solvers - continuation methods - similarity and scaling analysis - finite-geometry COMSOL models - yielded / unyielded region analysis - systematic comparison with prior literature
ADD: one clean Bn–Re regime map or 1D vs COMSOL comparison
## Coupled Fluid–Particle Heat Transfer Built an ANSYS Fluent + Discrete Phase Method model for heat and momentum transfer in a serpentine microtube. The model examined single-phase and dilute particle-laden cases, including two-way momentum and energy coupling.
ADD: serpentine geometry + velocity / temperature or particle-track contour
**Topics:** CFD, DPM, laminar/turbulent transport, particle trajectories, heat transfer, mesh comparison. ## Corrosion Under Insulation Modeling Developed COMSOL finite-element models for oxygen transport and corrosion in thin electrolyte films relevant to corrosion-under-insulation environments. **Topics:** diffusion, electrochemical transport, multiphysics coupling, thin-film modeling. ## Research Infrastructure As the first PhD student in a newly established research group, I have also contributed to building the research environment itself: - equipment procurement and commissioning - laboratory safety and operating procedures - instrument maintenance and vendor support - custom experimental setup development - undergraduate research mentoring This operational experience is an important part of how I approach research engineering: a model or experiment is useful only if it can be implemented, validated, and maintained.
